hints.title: Taller Observer Occlusion Obstacle
hints.text: A taller person completely blocks the view of everyone behind them. How can traversing people from right to left and maintaining a decreasing sequence of visible heights count visible persons in amortized O(1)?

hints.title: Reverse Monotonic Visibility Invariant
hints.text: For person i, all people in the sequence shorter than heights[i] are visible and subsequently occluded. If someone taller remains in the sequence, they are also visible, but no one behind them can be seen.

hints.title: Backward Height Occlusion Procedure
hints.text: Initialize answer array of size N to 0 and an empty height list. Iterate i from n - 1 down to 0: while the height list is non-empty and heights[i] > list[-1], pop height and increment answer[i]. If the list is still non-empty, increment answer[i] by 1 (the taller blocker). Push heights[i] to list. Return answer.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of persons in heights array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Each person is pushed and popped at most once during reverse traversal.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning rightward from each person until hitting a taller person takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining the visible skyline in an auxiliary list limits total operations to strictly O(N).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Realizing that people who are shorter than current height are visible and become blocked from earlier viewers.
